function: Over-the-air gradient aggregation for federated learning across a MIMO multiple-access channel: sparse-coded multiplexing with optimized precoding and post-processing matrices to minimize aggregation error (pp. 2, 4-5, 9).
system: Uplink MIMO: PS with 16 receive antennas, 20 devices with 8 transmit antennas each (other sizes tested), block fading, no RIS, band not stated (pp. 3, 10, 13).
method: Non-learned transceiver (sparse coding, partial-DFT compression, Turbo-CS recovery, AO-KKT precoding); the learned model is a CNN or ResNet18 trained by federated SGD over the air (pp. 4-6, 9-11).
data_channel: Simulated block-fading channel with i.i.d. CN(0,1) entries and distance path loss; FMNIST and CIFAR-10 for the FL task; no channel dataset or measurements (pp. 10-11).
test_conditions: FL trained and tested under the same simulated channel statistics; sweeps of noise power, streams, antennas and devices, with i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. data splits (pp. 3, 11-12).
baselines: Zero-forcing [26], antenna selection [27], AO-based beamforming [23], Turbo-CS with beamforming [18], GBMA [57]; ablations without compression or sparse coding; CVX and ADMM solvers; error-free (pp. 11-14).
metrics: Test accuracy, compressed gradient aggregation MSE, and number of channel uses needed to reach an accuracy level (pp. 11-14).
complexity: O(Imax(M N^3 log(1/eps) + N^3)) for the AO-KKT design with N = max{NT, NR, NS}, versus O(N^7 log(1/eps)) for interior point (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 10: "i.i.d. drawn from CN (0, 1)" - custom channel (path loss times an i.i.d. Gaussian matrix, textbook reference [51]); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 3: "the channel statistics remain unchanged throughout the entire training process" - the FL model is trained and tested under the same channel statistics; the sweeps of noise power, streams, antennas and devices (pp. 11-12) involve no train/test shift, fine-tuning or transfer.
q3_support: p. 13: "zero-forcing [26], antenna selection [27], AO-based beamforming [23] and Turbo-CS & beamforming [18]" - earlier published OA-FL designs (zero-forcing is the simple non-learned one), compared on test accuracy against channel uses; p. 14 says SCoM reaches the highest learning accuracy in all cases.
q4_support: p. 10: "Therefore, the overall complexity of Algorithm 1 is given by" O(Imax(M N^3 log(1/eps) + N^3)) - order of the proposed AO-KKT design; Table III (p. 13) lists parameters and channel uses, which do not count.
q5_support: p. 11: "We train our network on two datasets: FMNIST [53]" - public datasets of the learning task only; the channel is simulated (p. 10) and no code or data link is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included under the federated-learning-over-the-air rule: the wireless design (sparse coding, Turbo-CS, AO-KKT precoding and post-processing) is not learned, and the learned element is the FL model (CNN1, CNN2, ResNet18, p. 11). Area 7 because the problem solved is the over-the-air gradient aggregation over a MIMO multiple-access channel (p. 2). The SISO case (p. 13, Fig. 11) is only an ablation; the main link is MIMO. q3: the baselines are earlier published aggregation designs plus classical zero-forcing, compared on test accuracy against channel uses (Fig. 13, p. 14). q4: the complexity counted is that of the transceiver design (p. 10), not the model size.
